propositions: Four deterministic, read-only metric functions must derive code-health measurements from git history and the working tree: module_size_distribution, cap_change_events, churn, and refactor_to_addition_ratio.

Each metric function must be wrapped in a single-arg adapter compute (pulling repo_root, since, until from context) and registered into REGISTRY with lens='code_health', source='git', confidence='high'.
module_size_distribution must scan src/rebar/**/*.py at a ref against the single-sourced cap in .github/module-size-limit.txt and return count, near_cap_count, over_cap_count, and max_loc.
cap_change_events must parse git log history of .github/module-size-limit.txt and return a list of {commit, old_limit, new_limit} dicts, or [] when no changes occurred in the range.
churn must sum insertions and deletions from git log --numstat over a range; refactor_to_addition_ratio must return deletions/insertions as a float, or None when insertions is 0.

Unit tests must validate exact values for module_size_distribution, churn, refactor_to_addition_ratio, and cap_change_events against fixture git repos; all four metric ids must be present in REGISTRY with correct labels.
